title: On the Pricing of Corporate Debt: The Risk Structure of Interest Rates
question: What is risky debt worth if the firm's assets follow a diffusion?
changed: Equity is a call on the firm's assets and risky debt is riskless debt minus a put: the structural model of default.
assumed: Default only at maturity, when assets fall below the face value of debt.

title: Valuing Corporate Securities: Some Effects of Bond Indenture Provisions
question: What if a firm can default before its debt matures?
changed: First-passage default: the firm defaults the first time assets hit a barrier set by covenants.

title: An equilibrium characterization of the term structure
question: What do bond prices look like if the short rate mean-reverts?
changed: A Gaussian Ornstein–Uhlenbeck short rate gives closed-form bond prices and the market price of interest-rate risk.
assumed: Gaussian rates, so they can go negative.

title: A Theory of the Term Structure of Interest Rates
question: Can the term structure be derived from a general equilibrium?
changed: The square-root (CIR) short rate: mean-reverting, non-negative, with volatility rising with the level and closed-form bond prices.

title: Term Structure Movements and Pricing Interest Rate Contingent Claims
question: Can a rates model take today's yield curve as given instead of explaining it?
changed: The first arbitrage-free model fitted exactly to the initial curve: a recombining tree of whole yield curves.

title: Parsimonious Modeling of Yield Curves
question: What is the smallest smooth curve that fits observed yields?
changed: Level, slope and curvature from three exponential components: the curve central banks still fit.

title: Pricing Interest-Rate-Derivative Securities
question: Can Vasicek and CIR be made to fit today's curve exactly?
changed: Time-dependent drift calibrates the short-rate models to the initial term structure while keeping them tractable.

title: Common Factors Affecting Bond Returns
question: How many independent forces move the yield curve?
changed: Three principal components, level, steepness and curvature, explain almost all bond return variation.

title: Bond Pricing and the Term Structure of Interest Rates: A New Methodology for Contingent Claims Valuation
question: What if you model the whole forward curve instead of the short rate?
changed: Under no-arbitrage the forward rates' drift is fixed by their volatilities: the HJM framework.

title: Pricing Derivatives on Financial Securities Subject to Credit Risk
question: Can default be priced without modeling the firm's balance sheet?
changed: Reduced-form credit: default is the first jump of a Poisson process with an intensity, priced like an interest rate.

title: A Yield-Factor Model of Interest Rates
question: Which multi-factor rate models keep bond yields linear in the factors?
changed: Characterized affine term-structure models, which nest Vasicek and CIR and price by solving Riccati equations.

title: The Market Model of Interest Rate Dynamics
question: Is there an arbitrage-free model in which caps price by Black's formula?
changed: The LIBOR market model: log-normal discrete forward rates, consistent with market quoting conventions.

title: Modeling Term Structures of Defaultable Bonds
question: Can defaultable bonds be priced with the same machinery as riskless ones?
changed: Discount at the short rate plus the loss rate: risky debt priced with a default-adjusted short rate.

title: On Default Correlation: A Copula Function Approach
question: How do you model many defaults happening together?
changed: Joined individual default times with a Gaussian copula; it became the CDO pricing standard, and its tails failed in 2008.
assumed: Gaussian dependence: no extra clustering of joint defaults in the tails.

title: Bond Risk Premia
question: Can excess bond returns be forecast?
changed: One tent-shaped combination of forward rates forecasts excess returns on bonds of every maturity.

title: Forecasting the term structure of government bond yields
question: Can the Nelson–Siegel factors be forecast?
changed: Dynamic Nelson–Siegel: model level, slope and curvature as time series and forecast the whole curve.
